subject: ROLLBACK statement
notes: General format is the single keyword ROLLBACK (cite.py --check 14.9.36.2 "ROLLBACK" -> OK, <u>ROLLBACK</u>). Grammar: rollbackFacilityStatement : ROLLBACK, reached from `statement` under {facilityWord("ROLLBACK")}? so it is a statement exactly where §8.9 reserves the word. Editions from the spec: Annex E.3.2 item 2 'Commit and rollback facility' (cite.py --check E.3.2 "Commit and rollback facility." -> OK §E.3.2 2)) - a COBOL-2023 addition; below 2023 ROLLBACK is a user word and there is no ROLLBACK statement. Probed on the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/rollback/rb9_2014.cob): a bare ROLLBACK statement compiles and runs at --std 2023, and at 85/2002/2014 is rejected as an undefined user word (COBOL1639) - correct, no such statement exists there. The goldens pin a bare ROLLBACK parsing as a statement in sentence and imperative positions. FMT under an unclaimed module: the derived selector commit-and-rollback-only excludes FMT rows by KIND and records that the shipped grammar matches the printed format, which this confirms.
